hints.content:
The measure of an arc is equal to the measure of the [[☃ definition 1]] that intercepts it.

The arc measure of $\stackrel{\large{\frown}}{CD}$ is the measure of $\angle CPD$. We need to find the measure of  $\angle CPD$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A circle that is centered around point P. Points A, B, C, D, and E all lie on this circle in a clockwise direction. Line segments A D and B E are diameters. Line segments A P, B P, C P, D P, and E P are radii of the circle. The angle A P E is a right angle. Angle D P E is a thirty-three K minus nine degree angle. The angle C P D is a twenty K plus four degree angle. Arc C D is highlighted.

hints.content:
From the diagram, we see that $\angle APE$ and $\angle EPD$ are supplementary.  The measures of supplementary angles add up to $180^\circ$.  Thus:

$\begin{align}
m\angle APE + m\angle EPD&=180
\\\\
90 + (33k-9)  &= 180
\\\\
81+ 33k &= 180
\\\\
33k &= 99
\\\\
k &= 3
\end{align}$.

We remember that we were trying find the measure of $\angle CPD$.  Let's substitute in our value for $k$.

$\begin{align}
m\angle CPD&=(20k+4)^\circ
\\\\
&= (20(3)+4)^\circ
\\\\
&=64^\circ
\end{align}$
